race_context: The district: South Adams Schools has its office at 1075 Starfire Way in Berne, Adams County, and runs an elementary, a middle and a high school {sa_home}. South Adams High School was formed by consolidating the Berne, Geneva, Hartford Township and Jefferson Township high schools, and it had 347 students in 2024–25, according to Wikipedia {wiki_sahs}. This guide did not find a current districtwide enrollment figure.

Superintendent: Superintendent Michelle Clouser Penrod announced in July 2025 that she would retire after the 2025–26 school year, and Meyer was selected to replace her {bw_penrod}. The district's notice for the Feb. 10, 2026 contract hearing summarized an agreement employing Joseph Meyer as superintendent from July 1, 2026, with a $118,000 base salary {sa_supt_notice}{sa_ag_feb26}. The district site lists Joe Meyer as superintendent {sa_home}.

The board: there are seven members, and each seat has a defined area {sa_board}. District I is west of County Road 000 and south of State Highway 218, not counting Berne and Geneva {sa_board}. District II is east of County Road 000 and south of SR 218, also not counting Berne and Geneva {sa_board}. District III is the City of Berne, District IV is the Town of Geneva, District V is north of SR 218 (not counting Berne), and District VI is at large {sa_board}. The members are President Arlene Amstutz (II, term ends 2028), Vice President Adam Lehman (III, 2026), Secretary Landon Patterson (I, 2026), Rhonda Briggs (IV, 2028), Brian Caffee (V, 2028), Kyle Litwiller (VI, 2028) and Mitch Sprunger (III, 2026) {sa_board}. At its first meeting of 2026, the board passed a motion to keep things the same for 2026 {bw_jan26}.

District 1 (one seat): this is a rematch {adams_2022}. In 2022 Landon Patterson defeated Benjamin M. Rediger 1,181 votes to 1,009 {adams_2022}. Patterson's term ends in 2026 {sa_board}. On the 2026 state list, Rediger is labeled Republican and Patterson Independent {in_list}.

District 3 (likely two seats): District III has two board members, Adam Lehman and Mitch Sprunger, and both terms end in 2026 {sa_board}. In 2022 the District 3 race was 'Vote For 2,' and Lehman (1,791 votes) and Mitchel W. Sprunger (1,338) were the only candidates {adams_2022}. The state list shows District 3 as 'vote for 1,' with Adam S Lehman (Republican) and Mitch Sprunger (Nonpartisan) {in_list}. If both seats are on the ballot, as in 2022, both incumbents would be elected. This guide did not find a 2026 sample ballot to confirm. Both District 3 candidates are sitting members {sa_board}.
How candidates qualified: school board candidates filed petitions with the county clerk by noon on June 18, 2026 {bw_filing}.

Budget and property taxes (2025–2026): the board approved its 2026 budget in October 2025 {bw_oct25}. For 2027, the district's budget notice lists a total of $19,635,361: $11,820,875 for Education, $4,257,211 for Operations, $2,357,275 for Debt Service and $1,200,000 for the Rainy Day fund {sa_budget27}. It also lists a property tax cap credit estimate of $539,000 and a maximum operating levy estimate of $3,739,580 {sa_budget27}. The hearing was set for Aug. 18, 2026 and adoption for Oct. 13, 2026 {sa_budget27}. The board held its 2027 budget workshop in July 2026 {bw_budget27}. This guide did not find district statements on how SEA 1 affects South Adams.

Facilities and bonds (2025–2026): in October 2025 the board approved phase 2 of its facility improvement project {bw_oct25}. In early 2026 the board discussed a sanitary project, auditorium lighting and upgrades, and authorizing and refinancing bonds {sa_ag_jan26}{sa_ag_feb26}{sa_ag_mar26}. The March 10, 2026 agenda included a review of bids for phase 2 of the sanitary project {sa_ag_mar26}. On April 14, 2026 it held a hearing on a '2026 Unified Project' covering renovations and improvements across the district, site work, and buying equipment, buses and technology {sa_unified_notice}{sa_ag_apr26}. That meeting's agenda included a project resolution and a declaration of intent to reimburse expenditures {sa_unified_notice}{sa_ag_apr26}. The board approved bids for summer projects in June 2026 and got construction updates in July {bw_bids}{bw_renov}. In August 2026 the district gave notice of a plan to issue about $7,780,000 in bonds to refinance its Series 2016 building corporation bonds {sa_bldg_corp}{sa_determination}.

Teachers (2025–2026): the board held a public hearing on teacher pay and bargaining on Sept. 9, 2025, and a hearing on a tentative teacher contract on Nov. 4, 2025 {sa_ag_sep25}{sa_ag_nov25}. The district has posted a tentative 2026–27 master contract {sa_home}.

Policies and scheduling (2026): the March and April 2026 agendas included retiring all of the district's NEOLA policies and approving the Indiana School Boards Association's required policies {sa_ag_mar26}{sa_ag_apr26}. A February 2026 Berne Witness report said the board was divided over synchronous e-learning while discussing the 2026–27 calendar {bw_sync}{sa_ag_feb26}. In June 2026 administrators told the board about an attendance policy updated to match state standards {bw_absence}. In April 2026 a resident used the guest comment time to object to a Turning Point USA club {bw_tpusa}.

School safety (2026): the board discussed a safety ordinance in January 2026 {sa_ag_jan26}. In May 2026 the school resource officer brought a traffic-enforcement ordinance for South Adams Schools to the Berne Board of Public Works and Safety {bw_ordinance}. In September 2026 the director of operations reported to the board on a mock disaster drill {bw_drill}.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forums, questionnaires or news profiles of the 2026 South Adams candidates.
